title: Full-Wave Bridge Rectifier: Both Halves of the Wave
topic: Full-wave bridge rectifier — four diodes arranged in a bridge route both halves of an AC sine wave through the load in the same direction; the output is the absolute value of the input, doubling the ripple frequency over a half-wave rectifier

beats.narration: A half-wave rectifier throws away half the input. Can we keep both halves and still get a one-sided output?

elements.content: Manimo enters centre-screen
Half the wave goes to waste — can we keep all of it?

beats.narration: Four diodes wired as a bridge. An AC source on one diagonal, a load on the other. Two diodes will conduct on the positive half, two on the negative.

elements.content: AC source symbol on the left
Bridge diamond with four diodes: D1 top-left, D2 top-right, D3 bottom-left, D4 bottom-right
Wires from AC source top to W (AC1), AC source bottom to E (AC2)
Wires from N (+) and S (−) to load on the right
Load resistor (vertical zigzag) on the right
Diode labels D1, D2, D3, D4
Output rails labelled + (top) and − (bottom)
four diodes, one AC source, one load

beats.narration: On the positive half, D1 and D4 conduct. Current flows out the top, through the load, back through the bottom. On the negative half, D2 and D3 take over — but the current through the load still flows top to bottom.

elements.content: Positive half: D1 and D4 highlighted amber, D2 and D3 dimmed
elements.note: alternates with negative half via useSprite localTime

elements.content: Negative half: D2 and D3 highlighted, D1 and D4 dimmed
Current dots animated along the conducting path for whichever half is active
State badge top: POSITIVE HALF / NEGATIVE HALF, alternating
Load arrow: I_LOAD ↓ — always pointing the same direction
two diodes swap in, two swap out — but the load current never reverses

beats.narration: Watch V in trace as a full sinusoid, and V out as the absolute value — every dip flipped above the line, so the ripple frequency is doubled.

elements.content: Two stacked scope panels: V_in (top) and V_out (bottom)
V_in trace — full sinusoid both halves, two periods
V_out trace — |sin(ωt)|, only positive humps, doubled frequency
Vertical time cursor sweeping across both panels in sync
Panel labels 'V_in' and 'V_out'
ripple frequency is doubled — half the smoothing capacitor needed

beats.narration: Both halves of the wave do useful work — that's why every wall-wart and laptop charger starts with a bridge.

elements.content: Every half-cycle counts.
the front end of every AC-to-DC power supply
